story: A consumer complaint must be filed within 6 months, right? I bought a defective fridge for Rs 32,000 on 1 April 2026 and the refund was refused on 20 April 2026.

timeline.event: Bought a defective fridge for Rs 32,000
timeline.user_words: I bought a defective fridge for Rs 32,000 on 1 April 2026
the refund was refused on 20 April 2026

facts.user_goal: Confirm if a consumer complaint must be filed within 6 months
missing: Name of the seller or company

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 20 Apr 2028 (529 days left). This counts 2 years from 20 Apr 2026 (the date they refused; if they refused earlier, your deadline is earlier). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.
rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 32,000, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

support.text: You have two years to file a consumer complaint.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states that complaints must be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose, directly supporting the two-year time limit.

support.text: The deadline is 20 April 2028 because the refund was refused on 20 April 2026.
support.reason: The law text states the period is two years from when the cause of action arose, but does not specify that the cause of action arose on the date of refund refusal. The sentence adds a factual assumption about when the cause of action arose that is not in the law text.

support.text: You can file the complaint in the District Consumer Commission because you paid Rs 32,000.
support.reason: The law text states District Commission has consideration up to Rs 50 lakh, and Rs 32,000 falls within this limit. The amount in the sentence is applied to the rule.

support.text: You can file the complaint in the District Consumer Commission because you paid Rs 32,000.
support.reason: The law text provides jurisdiction rules based on where the opposite party resides, carries on business, has a branch office, or where the cause of action arises, or where the complainant resides. It does not mention the amount paid as a basis for determining which District Commission to file in.

support.text: You can file the complaint in the District Consumer Commission because you paid Rs 32,000.
support.reason: The law text provides rules for who may file a complaint, not where to file it based on the amount paid. The sentence incorrectly applies the pecuniary jurisdiction rule to the filing location.

support.text: There is no filing fee because the amount is up to Rs 5 lakh.
support.reason: The law text mentions electronic filing but does not specify the website e-jagriti.gov.in. The sentence adds a specific website that is not in the law text.

Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On 01 April 2026 I paid Rs 32,000 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests, including on 20 April 2026, you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 32,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
